{"notes":"Analysis 2026-11-25: VALID against current code, and it is a consequence of PKIX-rm8.29 / PKIX-wnnn.5 rather than an independent problem. P1 -> P2 and should be done with them.

Verified the mechanism rather than the line numbers (which have moved; the logic now lives in pkix-chain/src/sans_io.rs):
- try_build calls build_first_valid_path and, on Err(NoValidPath { .. }), returns PoolVerdict::OnlyUnvalidated -- DISCARDING the tried count and last_error, literally via `{ .. }` (sans_io.rs:319).
- assemble_unvalidated then calls pkix_path_builder::build_path (sans_io.rs:337), and the caller re-validates whatever that returns.

The beads worry -- that build_path may return a DIFFERENT chain than the one NoValidPath came from -- is not merely possible, it is structurally guaranteed to be possible. build_first_valid_path passes Some(verifier) to PathCandidates::new, so its candidates are signature-pruned. build_path takes no verifier at all and passes None (pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:1010). So build_path can return a chain whose signatures do not verify, which build_first_valid_path would never have yielded as a candidate. The error the caller finally sees can therefore describe a chain that was never among those tried.

The important part: this fallback exists ONLY because NoValidPath carries its error as a String. The in-code rationale says so in as many words -- "hand it over so the caller sees the real defect instead of no path found", and at the depth cap, "the caller learns what is wrong with the certificates rather than that we ran out of fetches". The whole manoeuvre is a workaround for an opaque field: throw away the stringly-typed error, rebuild a chain by topology alone, and re-validate it just to obtain a structured pkix_path::Error.

So type NoValidPath.last_error and this fallback can be DELETED, not fixed. The caller gets a structured error from the attempt that actually happened, on the chain that actually failed, and the divergence disappears because nothing is rebuilt.

That is now unblocked: pkix_path::Error gained Hash in 000ac209 (the obstacle was a single non-Hash variant, Der(DerError), whose Hash is four lines over the field its hand-written PartialEq already compares). See the notes on rm8.29 / wnnn.5.

Nothing to do here in isolation. PoolVerdict is crate-private so carrying the payload through it would be free, but there is no point plumbing a String further when the fix is to stop it being a String. Sequence: type the field, then delete assemble_unvalidated and the OnlyUnvalidated arm.","priority":2}

Fixed as a consequence of typing NoValidPath.last_error (PKIX-rm8.29 / PKIX-wnnn.5), exactly as the analysis predicted: the fallback was deleted rather than repaired.

The bead concern was that when build_first_valid_path returns NoValidPath, pkix-chain fell back to topology-only build_path and returned THAT chain, so the error the caller finally saw could describe a different chain than the one that failed. Confirmed structurally guaranteed to be possible, not hypothetical: build_first_valid_path passes Some(verifier) to PathCandidates::new, so its candidates are signature-pruned, while build_path passes None (pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:1010). build_path can therefore return a chain whose signatures do not verify and that the iterating builder never yielded.

The whole manoeuvre existed only because last_error was a rendered String -- the in-code rationale said so: "hand it over so the caller sees the real defect instead of no path found". So: throw away the opaque error, rebuild by topology alone, re-validate, just to obtain a structured pkix_path::Error.

With the field typed, PoolVerdict::OnlyUnvalidated carries the builder own error and both use sites (the depth cap and the exhausted-URIs path) report it directly. assemble_unvalidated is gone. The caller now gets the failure from the attempt that actually ran, on the chain that actually failed, and the divergence cannot occur because nothing is rebuilt.

Test: a_wrong_key_intermediate_reports_the_typed_validation_failure in pkix-chain/tests/review_aia.rs pins PathBuild(NoValidPath) with a SignatureInvalid cause.

Incidental finding while writing it, filed separately: absorb() reports Error::Aia(AiaError::FetchingDisabled) whenever a fetch adds no new certificate -- including when the fetch SUCCEEDED and merely returned something already pooled. FetchingDisabled is untrue in that case.
